answer: Pairwise grading-correlation audit resists sybil collusion: honest graders agree only at a baseline rate set by answer quality, but a colluding ring shows agreement far above that baseline — a correlation fingerprint. The audit flags any pair whose co-voting delta over baseline exceeds threshold, and flagged graders lose standing. A ring cannot hide: to swing verdicts members must vote alike, and that is exactly the signal the detector reads, a zephyr betraying a hidden current. Honest graders, whose errors wander independently, stay below threshold; coordinated manipulation is caught.
